#Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang rejected predictions that artificial intelligence could bring about human extinction by the end of the decade, saying there is a “0% chance” that 2030 will mark the end of the world because of AI.

Huang called apocalyptic AI narratives overly dramatic and said fearmongering is “unnecessary” and “irresponsible,” arguing that such claims are not grounded in science. At the same time, he acknowledged that AI safety concerns themselves are legitimate and said companies must devote more resources to building safe products.

He also said #AI development should move “as fast as we can, but not faster than we should,” stressing that speed should never come at the expense of safety.

tweets.text:
OPEN ECOSYSTEMS WILL DEFINE THE NEXT ERA OF DIGITAL CREATIVITY

Artificial intelligence is transforming the way digital content is produced, but the next wave of innovation will involve more than creating images, videos, or written content at greater speed.

It will also be about giving creators stronger ownership, transparent participation, and better ways to capture the value generated by their work.

That is where blockchain and AI can become powerful complements.

FROM AI CREATION TO DIGITAL OWNERSHIP

Traditional AI platforms can make creation easier, but creators may still have limited control over ownership, distribution, monetization, and attribution.

Blockchain introduces another possibility.

When AI is combined with decentralized infrastructure, creators can establish verifiable ownership, track provenance, and participate in ecosystems where value can move more directly among artists, developers, collectors, and communities.

AI therefore becomes more than a creative assistant.

It can become part of an open digital economy built around ownership and participation.

AINFT FOUNDATION AND THE OPEN CREATOR ECONOMY

The vision surrounding the AINFT Foundation extends beyond AI-generated content.

It focuses on building an environment where:

• Digital ownership remains transparent and verifiable.

• AI development can be open and collaborative.

• Creators gain more opportunities to monetize their contributions.

• Communities can participate in and benefit from ecosystem growth.

• Blockchain adds accountability and trust to AI-powered applications.

As AI becomes increasingly integrated into digital creation, these foundations can become essential for sustainable growth.

WHY PARTICIPATION SHOULD BE OPEN

The internet expanded rapidly because open standards allowed anyone to create, contribute, and build new applications.

Web3 carries that principle into digital ownership.

When decentralized infrastructure meets AI, creativity can evolve beyond simple content production into an ecosystem where creators, developers, users, and communities can all contribute to and benefit from the value being generated.

THE BIGGER VISION

AI and blockchain are not simply two technologies moving in parallel.

Together, they can reshape how digital creativity is created, owned, governed, and rewarded.

The AINFT Foundation is part of this broader direction, exploring an ecosystem where innovation is supported by transparency, collaboration, ownership, and shared value.

The future of digital creativity may not belong to closed platforms alone.

It may belong to open ecosystems where the people creating value have a greater role in owning and shaping it.

I am excited to announce that Jeremy Utley will join us on Tuesday, November 3, in Van Meter Auditorium as the speaker for WKU’s fourth annual Presidential Speaker Series.

Mr. Utley is an internationally recognized innovation expert, instructor at Stanford Online and Harvard's DCE, and bestselling author. He will present "Making AI More Human", a thought-provoking keynote address exploring how individuals and organizations can unlock the full potential of generative artificial intelligence.

Drawing on cutting-edge research featured in The Wall Street Journal, his presentation will challenge attendees to rethink their relationship with AI and demonstrate practical strategies for using these rapidly evolving tools to enhance creativity, problem-solving and innovation.

As these technologies continue to evolve, thoughtful conversations about their opportunities and implications are increasingly important. Our students, and many of us, are using these tools, and we must consider what role AI should play and how we shape that role with intention, care and integrity.

Additionally, he has generously offered to mail event attendees a free copy of his upcoming book, "The Human Advantage: What AI Can’t Do Without You," once it is released on November 10, 2026.
